# Crew API: grants (Owner endpoints)

Part of the [Crew API reference](README.md).

## GET /v1/crew/owner/grants

List grants (with usage).

| About | This endpoint |
|---|---|
| Status | Available now: owner only |
| Tier | Owner |
| Stability | stable |
| Callers the API defines | The owner, with the owner's own sign-in. |

revoked grants are not listed by default. Served for grants made through local authorization (amendment, 2026-11-24), oldest first. Such a grant is active or gone, so any other `status` lists nothing; each row carries `kind`, `namespace`, `client_id`, `app`, `scopes`, `status`, `created_at` and `expires_at`.

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|

| `limit` | integer (1 to 100, default `20`) | no |  |

| `X-Request-Id` | string | no | A caller may supply its own; an id assigned by an intermediary in front of the gateway wins. |

## PATCH /v1/crew/owner/grants/{grant_id}

|---|---|
| Status | Planned |

| Stability | stable |

## DELETE /v1/crew/owner/grants/{grant_id}

Revoke a grant.

| About | This endpoint |
|---|---|
| Status | Available now: owner only |
| Tier | Owner |
| Stability | stable |
| Callers the API defines | The owner, with the owner's own sign-in. |

Takes effect locally first (status=revoked), then the issuer of the grant is told over the control channel. Open streams receive grant.revoked and are closed. For a grant made through local authorization (amendment, proposed), the host owner's credential is required and Shared Crew teammates and app tokens receive 403 owner_only; every access and refresh token under the grant is refused from the next request; a second call answers the same 200 until the grant's own expiry, then 404. Such a grant has no outside issuer to tell.

Path parameters:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `grant_id` | string | yes | grt_ id |

Request headers:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Crew-API-Version` | string | no | The minor version the client was written for. Without it, the server answers with 1.0 behaviour. The server never refuses a request because this version is old. |
| `X-Request-Id` | string | no | A caller may supply its own; an id assigned by an intermediary in front of the gateway wins. |

Response `200`: Success.

Response headers:

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `X-Request-Id` | string | One id per request, supplied by the caller or an intermediary, or generated by the gateway. Also written to the audit log and the error body. |
| `Crew-API-Version` | string | The server's minor version, for example 1.3. |

|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | yes |  |
| `object` | string | no |  |
| `deleted` | `true` | yes |  |

## POST /v1/crew/owner/grants/{grant_id}/resume

Resume a paused or throttled grant.

| About | This endpoint |
|---|---|
| Status | Planned |
| Tier | Owner |
| Stability | stable |
| Callers the API defines | The owner, with the owner's own sign-in. |

paused or throttled goes back to active. A grant with pause.by=reconsent gets 409 and recovers only through a new consent; one with pause.by=entitlement gets 409 and recovers by itself when the app's entitlement is back.

## GET /v1/crew/owner/grants/{grant_id}/decisions

Read the monitor's decision log.

| About | This endpoint |
|---|---|
| Status | Planned |
| Tier | Owner |
| Stability | stable |
| Callers the API defines | The owner, with the owner's own sign-in. |

Reads this grant's monitor decisions, newest first. The shape is the same whichever kind of decider is used: decided_by says whether a rule or a model decided, and decider gives its version. Retention: monitor decisions are kept 30 days by default; the owner can set `crew_api.retention_days` in the crew settings to 1 to 365 days.
